html:
When the holiday table is set, a little extra flavor can turn an ordinary dinner into a memorable feast. One of the simplest ways to add depth is by making DIY herb infused butter for holiday dinner. With the right tools—like the Herb Scissors, a five‑blade set of herb shears—you can mince fresh cilantro, chives, and basil in seconds, then fold them into softened butter for a bright, aromatic spread.

Why DIY Herb Infused Butter Beats Store‑Bought Versions

Store‑bought herb butter often contains preservatives, excess salt, or dried herbs that lose their punch. By creating your own, you control the ingredients, texture, and intensity. Fresh herbs give a vibrant green color and a garden‑fresh aroma that complements roasted turkey, mashed potatoes, and warm rolls. Plus, the process is fast enough to fit into a busy holiday prep schedule.

Essential Tools and Ingredients

Gather these items before you start:

  • 1 cup unsalted butter, softened (room temperature)
  • 2 tablespoons fresh cilantro, stems removed
  • 2 tablespoons fresh chives, trimmed
  • 2 tablespoons fresh basil leaves
  • 1 teaspoon lemon zest (optional for brightness)
  • Sea salt and freshly cracked black pepper to taste
  • Herb Scissors – five‑blade herb shears that mince cilantro, chives, and basil in one snip, complete with a cleaning comb

The Herb Scissors are the star of this recipe. Their five blades slice herbs cleanly, preserving color and preventing bruising that can happen with a regular knife. The built‑in cleaning comb makes it easy to clear any stuck pieces, so you stay efficient throughout the holiday rush.

Step‑By‑Step: Making the Butter

  1. Prep the butter. Place the softened butter in a medium bowl. Use a rubber spatula to smooth out any lumps, creating a creamy base.
  2. Harvest the herbs. Rinse cilantro, chives, and basil under cold water. Pat dry with a kitchen towel or a salad spinner. Removing excess moisture is crucial; too much water will make the butter watery.
  3. Trim and gather. Snap off the cilantro stems, discard the thickest parts, and stack the tender leaves. Trim the chives to a few inches and gather the basil leaves.
  4. Use the Herb Scissors. Open the five‑blade Herb Scissors and place a handful of each herb inside the blades. One quick snip will produce uniform, fine pieces. Repeat until you have roughly 2‑3 teaspoons of each herb minced.
  5. Combine. Sprinkle the minced herbs over the butter. Add lemon zest, a pinch of sea salt, and a few cracks of black pepper. Fold the mixture together using the spatula, ensuring the herbs are evenly distributed.
  6. Shape and chill. Transfer the butter onto a piece of parchment paper. Roll it into a log, twist the ends, and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes. The chilled butter can be sliced into rounds for serving.

Using the Herb Scissors eliminates the need for a cutting board and a knife, reducing prep time and keeping your herbs brighter. The clean, even cut also means the butter stays smooth rather than turning gritty.For a visual cue, the butter should have a pale green swirl throughout. If you prefer a stronger herb presence, simply increase the amount of minced herbs before shaping the log.

Creative Ways to Use Your Holiday Butter

Once the butter has set, it becomes a versatile condiment:

  • Finish roasted vegetables. A warm slice melted over carrots, Brussels sprouts, or sweet potatoes adds an instant burst of freshness.
  • Flavor the turkey. Slip a butter pat under the skin of the turkey before roasting; the herb‑infused steam keeps the meat moist and aromatic.
  • Spread on warm bread. Serve rounds of butter alongside dinner rolls or a crusty baguette for guests to enjoy.
  • Enhance mashed potatoes. Stir a spoonful into creamy potatoes for a subtle herbal note that cuts through richness.

Because the butter is homemade, you can also experiment with additional flavors—think roasted garlic, smoked paprika, or a splash of white wine—without worrying about hidden additives.

Cleaning Up: Keeping Your Herb Scissors Ready for Next Use

The built‑in cleaning comb on the Herb Scissors makes maintenance a breeze. After you finish mincing, tap the blades gently to dislodge larger pieces, then run the comb through the blades to clear any remaining bits. Rinse under warm water and dry thoroughly. Storing the scissors in a drawer with the comb attached prevents rust and keeps the blades sharp for future holiday projects.

Tips for Perfect Holiday Butter

Even with a simple recipe, a few tricks can elevate the result:

  • Softened, not melted. Butter that is too soft can become oily when mixed with herbs. Aim for a consistency similar to ripe avocado.
  • Season gradually. Add salt and pepper a little at a time, tasting as you go. Fresh herbs can be salty, so you may need less than you think.
  • Use fresh herbs. Older herbs lose potency. If you bought them a few days ago, give them a quick sniff—if the aroma is faint, consider re‑freshing with a splash of water.
  • Freeze for later. Wrap the butter log tightly in plastic wrap and freeze for up to three months. Thaw in the refrigerator before the next holiday season.

FAQ

Can I use dried herbs instead of fresh?

While you can substitute dried herbs, the flavor won’t be as bright and the texture will be grainy. Fresh cilantro, chives, and basil minced with the Herb Scissors give the best result for holiday butter.

How long does the butter keep in the fridge?

Stored in an airtight container, the herb infused butter stays fresh for about 5‑7 days. The herbs may lose some color over time, but the flavor remains enjoyable.

Is the Herb Scissors suitable for other herbs like parsley or dill?

Absolutely. The five‑blade design works well with most tender herbs. For tougher stems, you may want to trim them first, but the scissors handle parsley, dill, mint, and even thyme leaves with ease.
